properties.decision:
OPTIONS
(a) A SERVER-SIDE OVERLAY PER BRANCH, over the one shared store. ⭐ RECOMMENDED. The shared server keeps, per (design, branch), an overlay holding only the branch-scoped records and properties (dec:which-design-records-belong-to-a-branch). A session's reads see shared ∪ its branch's overlay; its branch-scoped writes go to its overlay; its measurement root is its worktree. Exporting a worktree writes shared ∪ that branch's overlay into THAT worktree's saved design. Intent written on any branch still goes live.
(b) AN AUTOMATIC WORKTREE-PRIVATE STORE: what the hub did by hand for #571, automated. Its facts are isolated, but intent written there has to be forwarded to the shared store, so there are two stores and a sync between them. That is the double-written-record conflict #571 hit, made systematic.
(c) A BRANCH TAG ON NODES IN THE ONE STORE. Cheapest to picture, but every read path must filter by tag forever, and an untagged read (any tool that forgets) leaks one branch's facts into another's answer silently.

RECOMMENDED (a), WITH THE LIFECYCLE STATED:
· CREATED on the first branch-scoped write from a session whose worktree is on a branch other than the default.
· FOLDED INTO the shared store when the branch's code reaches main. Detect it by CONTENT, not git ancestry (this project squash-merges): main's committed saved design now carries those facts, or the branch head's tree is contained in main. Folding is idempotent.
· ABANDONED when the branch is deleted unmerged: the overlay is retired, never folded, and its facts stay readable as history.
· On main itself there is no overlay; writes go straight to shared, as today.
· PERSISTED beside the store (per-branch files under .reflow2/), so a server restart does not lose in-flight branch facts.

═══ 2026-09-30 — BRAINSTORM NOTE (recorded as brainstorming; nothing chosen) ═══
@ajs asked for "ideas to counteract" this, as it was put against moving reflow2's design to flo2.io: "With one hosted design, every branch writes into the shared design before merge. Parallel branches see each other's half-done records, and an abandoned PR leaves records for code that never shipped." THIS NODE IS THE ANSWER, designed 2026-09-23 and still waiting for his word. Option (a)'s lifecycle (created per branch, folded by content at merge, retired unfolded if the branch dies) removes both halves of that objection.

WHAT HOSTING CHANGES (not covered above, which assumed a local shared server):
- On flo2.io the server cannot see a session's worktree or its git branch. So the BRANCH must be DECLARED by the caller. reflow2's local client (`--remote`) knows the branch and can send it, and flo2's gateway must pass it through, as it already passes the caller and the calling agent (flo2 #106).
- Fold-on-merge "detected by content" needs main's committed copy or the merged tree, which only a client or CI holds. So the fold is triggered from CI or the client, not discovered by the server.
- A chat-app session has no branch, and writes to shared, as on main.

A FOURTH OPTION, from what the 2026-09-29/30 fix agents actually did:
(d) DESIGN CHANGES TRAVEL WITH THE PR AS A REPLAYABLE SCRIPT. A branch writes NOTHING to the shared design. Its records are a list of tool calls kept in the PR (the agents' *-records.py / *-branch-records.sh). Mid-branch they are replayed into a scratch store seeded from the shared design, so the agent can read its own state. At merge, the same script is replayed once against the shared design. An abandoned PR is never replayed.
- FOR: no overlay machinery, nothing to retire, reviewers see exactly what the PR will write, and it works on flo2.io today.
- AGAINST:
  - A replay can fail or mean something else if main moved the nodes it touches. Most calls are upserts, but not all.
  - The script is code a reviewer reads instead of nodes.
  - Mid-branch it IS (b)'s private store, minus the forward-sync that made (b) conflict on #571.
- SIZE: small. The practice exists, so the work is a convention plus a replay step in the merge or CI. (a) is larger, server-side, and gives a live view of in-flight branches, which (d) cannot.
properties.name: DESIGN — where a branch's implementation facts are held until its code merges: a server-side overlay per branch, an automatic per-worktree store, or a branch tag on nodes?
properties.rationale: Designed 2026-09-23 on Anthony's instruction. PROPOSED for his word. (a) keeps one process and one store, which dec:multi-writer-architecture and the single-writer guarantee assume, and it is the only option where "intent live, facts per branch" holds by construction, not by discipline. (b) was measured the hard way on #571: the same ChangeEvent written to both stores conflicted on merge. Detecting a fold by content is required, not a preference: after a squash-merge the branch head is not an ancestor of main.
